q1_issues.issue: popular_subject_for_tv_movies fuses an incidental-description adjective plus a head noun plus that noun's PP argument into one symbol, which no compound rule licenses (the sensitive_to_light fusion is adjective-headed with a bare-kind complement, and "popular subject" is the "dented pail" incidental-description case).
"TV movies" never appears as a symbol anywhere, so the aboutness the sentence actually states is unqueryable and the tv_movie compound genus is missing.
The decomposition emits only the genus subject, leaving popular and the for-argument unexposed, so the fused symbol is not unpacked to single-word parts as Compound concepts requires.

q2_gaps: a kind-level predicate NOMINAL carrying its own PP argument ("Ns are a subject for Q") — the kind-level fusion rule covers adjective + bare-kind complements only, and the reified-state route under Complements of nouns and adjectives is for individuated bearers, so there is no licensed encoding for a bare-kind subject with a noun predicate that takes a for-argument
notes: The hit_man compound genus (noun modifier not exposed) and the bare-plural generic routing are right. KindProperty reads against the stated test (an individual can be a popular subject for TV movies) but is defensible for this category-level predication.
